en.title: What Is Pre-emption in Bangladesh?
en.directAnswer: Pre-emption is a legal right that may allow an eligible person to ask for a transferred property interest to be transferred to them instead. It is not available to everyone. Eligibility, the kind of land, the relationship to the holding, time limits and required deposits can all matter.

atAGlance.whoFor: A co-sharer or nearby interest holder wants to know whether they can challenge a transfer.
atAGlance.mainRule: Pre-emption is a legal right that may allow an eligible person to ask for a transferred property interest to be transfer
atAGlance.updateStatus: DEADLINE-SENSITIVE. Do not publish numeric limitation guidance without a lawyer checking the current text and case law.

en.lawMeaning:
Section 96 contains a statutory pre-emption framework. It also states that the section does not take away a right of pre-emption under Mohammedan law.

This page gives a general route. A person’s exact rights can change because of facts, documents, deadlines, legal status, court orders or later amendments.
steps: Identify the transferred land and deed.
Confirm your legal relationship to the holding.
Check the date you received notice or knowledge.
Calculate the legal filing deadline with a lawyer.
Check required deposits and court process.
evidence: Relevant official notices, receipts, and correspondence
en.simpleExample: A person hears that a co-sharer sold land to an outsider. That does not automatically mean the person has a valid pre-emption claim. The exact legal status and deadline must be checked.
en.specialistTrigger: Any intended pre-emption claim. This is deadline-sensitive litigation.
